title: Career Roadmap: Quant Analyst
summary: Use mathematics, statistics, programming and financial theory to analyse markets, develop quantitative models, measure financial risk and support investment, trading and portfolio-management decisions.

blocks.text: Use mathematics, statistics, programming and financial theory to analyse markets, develop quantitative models, measure financial risk and support investment, trading and portfolio-management decisions.

rows.text: Mathematics is strongly recommended; Statistics, Economics and Computer Science are useful
BS in Economics / Finance, B.Sc. Statistics, Mathematics, Economics or B.Tech. Computer Science
Quantitative finance, financial econometrics, algorithmic trading, risk modelling or portfolio analytics
M.Sc. Financial Mathematics, Quantitative Finance, Statistics, Mathematics or a related field

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: A BS in Economics or Finance can provide a foundation, but many quantitative roles require advanced mathematics, probability, statistics and programming. A mathematically rigorous curriculum is especially important for quant research and algorithmic trading.

blocks.label: Mathematics
blocks.text: Linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics and optimization.

blocks.label: Programming
blocks.text: Python, NumPy, pandas and SciPy; C++ can be valuable for performance-sensitive roles.

blocks.label: Financial Knowledge
blocks.text: Derivatives, bonds, equities, portfolio theory and market microstructure.

blocks.label: Quantitative Methods
blocks.text: Regression, time-series analysis, stochastic processes and numerical methods.

blocks.label: Data & Tools
blocks.text: SQL, financial datasets, backtesting frameworks and version control.

blocks.label: Risk & Validation
blocks.text: Model assumptions, overfitting, stress testing and performance evaluation.
Build three or four rigorous projects:

blocks.label: Portfolio Optimization
blocks.text: Compare portfolio allocations using risk and return measures.

blocks.label: Time-Series Forecasting
blocks.text: Analyse financial data and evaluate forecast performance against simple baselines.

blocks.label: Trading Strategy Backtest
blocks.text: Test a rules-based strategy while accounting for transaction costs and look-ahead bias.

blocks.label: Risk Modelling
blocks.text: Estimate volatility, drawdowns and Value at Risk (VaR) using historical data.

blocks.label: Options Pricing
blocks.text: Implement a basic Black–Scholes model and test how prices change with its assumptions.
Document the mathematical approach, data sources, assumptions, validation methods and limitations. Avoid presenting backtested returns as guaranteed future performance.
Target roles at:

items.text: Quantitative trading and proprietary trading firms.
Risk analytics and financial consulting firms.
Research teams at universities and financial research organisations.

blocks.text: Search for Quantitative Research Intern, Quant Analyst Intern, Risk Analytics Intern, Financial Modelling Intern and Trading Analytics Intern positions.
Prioritize:
CFA or FRM study may be useful for certain finance or risk roles, but neither replaces the mathematical and programming depth expected in many quant positions.
Quant / Risk Analytics Intern
Junior Quant Analyst / Quantitative Developer
Quant Analyst / Quantitative Researcher
Senior Quant → Quant Research Lead / Portfolio Strategist
Quantitative developer, quant researcher and risk quant are related but distinct paths with different technical requirements.

items.text: Investment banks and global financial institutions
Quantitative trading and proprietary trading firms

rows.text: Strengthen probability, statistics, linear algebra and Python fundamentals.
Study financial instruments and implement a portfolio or options-pricing model.
Complete a backtesting or risk-modelling project, document results and practise quantitative interviews.

blocks.label: Target-ready profile
blocks.text: Strong mathematical reasoning, Python programming, financial-market knowledge, statistical modelling and a validated quantitative project portfolio.
